PL3 — Finite kernel formula and actual bilinear period
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: A covariant kernel acts by the stabilizer-weighted finite orbit sum. Chains compose such maps, with a final coupled finite sum where applicable. The final period is the stabilizer-weighted sum of the normalized bilinear Fock pairing of br_u applied to the terminal column value with the row value. colPer_eq identifies this concrete period with the chain-factorized abstract period.

PL4 — Ramified source space, lattice, and retained rank
Historical/component status: faithful_translation

PL5 — Selected row space and projected row lattice
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The good row subspace is selected by the product of the finite-group character projector and level-character projector. Mt is the pointwise Nab lattice intersected with this subspace. Pq is the hermitian orthogonal projection to the selected rational theta-adjoint part in coordinates. The quotient lattice is Pq(Mt); the intersection lattice cutZ is a distinct object.
Assumptions: ["Metric positivity and the source rationality/stability assumptions for the selected subspaces."]
Depends on: ["PL1", "PL2"]
Source relation: The 1/|P| row metric normalization is retained. Auxiliary finite-group characters are not the outer Dirichlet target character.

PL8 — Rationalizing the complex scalar, including zero periods
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Given xi sigma(P)=sigma(B composed with iota pi), choose eta=xi^{-1} over K when xi lies in sigma(K). If xi does not lie in sigma(K), every period value vanishes, since a nonzero one expresses xi as a quotient of two K-values; then eta=1 works. The MIUnit2 finite-place assumption makes eta a unit at the selected place, without requiring B nonzero.
Assumptions: ["The complex comparison identity; xi is nonzero and its base value is 1; any K-preimage of xi at the selected parameter is a finite-place unit."]
Depends on: ["PL6", "PL7", "PL15"]
Source relation: The scalar in PairingFactorsThroughPeriods is the inverse of the scalar in MatrixIdentityOffBase; the main fragment tracks this inversion.

PL9 — Explicit common row lattice, fullness and uniqueness
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: R is the intersection over finite places of the localizations of iota_{mu(w)} pi_{mu(w)} Mt. Because mu is the base parameter outside finitely many places, all local modules can be glued into a full O_K-lattice; its localizations are exactly prescribed, and it is unique. A complete proof by primary decomposition of a finite torsion module is supplied.
Assumptions: ["Full Mt; surjective pi_t; bijective iota_t; finite exceptional set for mu."]
Depends on: ["PL5", "PL6"]
Source relation: Our proof uses standard primary decomposition of finite torsion O_K-modules. Localizations are inside the rational vector space, not completions.

PL10 — Shifted integral maps into the one common dual lattice
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: If local periods have ord_w at least sigma_u(w) unless zero, and their rational comparison scalar is a w-unit, then B_u(I_u N_u,R) is integral for I_u=product p_w^{-floor sigma_u(w)}. More generally the result holds for any finitely supported integer k_u(w)<=ceil sigma_u(w). The same R is independent of u.
Assumptions: ["Full source lattice; finite support of shifts; local period valuation bound; eta a local unit; exact row localizations."]
Depends on: ["PL8", "PL9", "PL12"]
Source relation: The zero alternative is kept explicitly. Allowing k<=ceil is already in the source; no claim is made that replacing every actual floor by ceil preserves all family records.

PL11 — Exact norm descent and the chain-height inequality
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Descent through a quotient with its quotient metric preserves functional norm. With final pairing bound p_v, chain operator bounds a_{j,v}, and lower squared norm factor s_v for the identification into the common metric space, ||B||_v^2<=p_v^2 product a_{j,v}^2/s_v. The source uses s_v=kappa_v min_p product_j lambda_{j,p,v}; taking the mean of logarithms preserves the order mean_v min_p. Logarithmic height is used only for B nonzero.
Assumptions: ["Positive definite metrics and quotient metric; the base chain factorization; positive norm majorants; p ranges over a finite nonempty spectral index set; kappa_v>0 and every lambda_{j,p,v}>0; spectral lower norm bound at every infinite place; B nonzero when ordinary logarithmic height is taken."]
Depends on: ["PL3", "PL7", "PL15"]
Source relation: The proof in the fragment is a compact human reconstruction. Quantitative kernel/eigenvalue estimates remain PL15. The source uses squared norms and equal means over infinite places in the totally complex setting.
Proof location: {"file": "period_lattice_section.tex", "anchors": ["eq:pl-norm", "eq:pl-height"]}

EL3 — Elementary row-degree bound by a generic block column operation
Historical/component status: derived_alternative_proof
Statement: For f in the column-invariant degree-nu module, every monomial has total degree at most sum_{i<=r}nu_i in the first r rows. Localize the generic matrix at the determinant of its top-left r-by-r block and kill the top-right block by earlier-column additions. The required upper-unipotent coefficients are independent of the row-scaling indeterminate, so the degree bound descends by injectivity of localization.

EL9 — The normalized neighbor sum sends ball sections to dual sections
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The actual operator is (Y_v F)(L)=p^A_v sum_{L'->L_v}F(L[v:=L']). Incoming edges form a finite set. Normalized edge integrality gives the tensor-valued slot inclusion termwise. Reindexing edges proves equivariance, and the zero-off-lattice condition is preserved. This proves RestNat with no A_v>=0 assumption.

EL10 — Normalized error transport used in the joint-rank cancellation
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For an edge e and c>=0, p^A(w^c R_e) subset w^c P_t(e.tgt). Thus a test vector vanishing to order w^c at an unwanted edge produces a normalized contribution in the corresponding w^c dual slot. When c>=2(D+1) this lies in p^(D+1)P_t; the source retains its stronger global cStar>=4(D+1) assumption.

SY5 — Finite cleaning with exact spare-exponent invariants
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For a key of order d<=2Q, a normal-degree-v error has coefficient w^x with x=max(d+1,v); E=x-d>=1 and v<=(2Q+1)E. Combining SY3/SY4 raises level by E while decreasing mu by (2Q+1)E and lambda by E. Initial ((2Q+3)c,c), level>=o, suffices to correct finitely to o+c while retaining off-plane vanishing. Projection preserves multidegree.
Remaining inputs: []
Source relation: Human source reconstruction; direct polynomial/coefficient arguments replace the source auxiliary graded-set bookkeeping where stated. No source change or Lean replay.

SY7 — Exact SPtrue multidegree and source budget
Historical/component status: faithful_translation

IP4 — Simultaneous integral adaptation to every prefix minimum and maximum
Historical/component status: derived_alternative_proof
Statement: Over an integral domain, the same integral basis is adapted to all source generic-conjugated rank-one prefix minimum/maximum bounds. The full-prefix converse isolates a maximal bad endpoint. Earlier prefixes follow from cutting the actual columns and counting continuations. Uniqueness intersects all prefix conditions, and fraction-field descent retains integral coefficients.

IP11 — Products of the actual column keys prove GeneratorImageIsSymbol
Historical/component status: derived_simplification

CL1 — An explicit complementary standard-monomial family
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: At a selected even twist use arrays e with e(0,0)=nu_0; at a selected odd twist use arrays with zero first row. Deleting respectively the first row/column or first row/last column identifies these with tail-shape arrays. Odd reversal gives lambda^0_2 minus the reversed original tail. Thus n2 is the product of D_(k-1)(tail) on selected twists and D_k(lambda^0) elsewhere.

CL4 — A short characteristic-zero operator-word theorem
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For H_d=Sym^d(F^k) in characteristic zero, an adjoint-stable subspace W of End(H_d) spanned by diagonal-weight vectors with all coordinates <=c lies in the span of words of length<=c in X_a partial_b. Highest vectors in End(H_d) are exactly X_1^j Y_k^j (sum X_iY_i)^(d-j). Complete reducibility gives one summand for each j. Applying the Fock commutator and row-degree bound puts every remainder contraction in c0-word closure, factor by factor.
Assumptions: ["F has characteristic zero.", "W is commutator-stable and spanned by simultaneous diagonal-weight vectors.", "Standard characteristic-zero complete reducibility of finite-dimensional rational GL_k representations.", "For the application, the remainder representation is spanned by bideterminants of width<=c0 and the Fock restriction is nondegenerate."]
Depends on: ["CL12"]
Source relation: New human proof via localization and highest weights; the source uses a different quadric-vanishing implementation. Neither integral coefficients of words nor integral semisimplicity are claimed. Lie stability plus torus weights is explicitly converted to GL stability before complete reducibility.

IN2 — Actual pair span, retained degree blocks and exact tensor factorization
Historical/component status: faithful_translation_with_elementary_exponent_proof
Statement: The actual localizer is supported on plane vector variables. The proof holds on BlockDeg-compatible blocks of each pair-product summand, extends by multilinearity to actual symbol-space factors, and then uses physical homogeneity to eliminate incompatible blocks. A compatible low-digit block factors as A_* tensor G_*, and normal coefficient extraction after the projector is a scalar multiple of A_*.

IN6 — Exact frame-digit identity and zero chain loss
Historical/component status: faithful_translation_with_explicit_monomial_proof
Statement: After expanding the independent lab variables, exact quotient/remainder arithmetic gives Fdig_sigma(X^beta phi Q)=0 or X^lift(floor(beta/P))Q for Q supported on ll,wc. The extra monomial contains only vector letters in each chain. Thus every frame-digit extraction retains the complete thStar chain bound.

IN8 — Exact degree cancellation and numerical bound Delta_j<=slU/8
Historical/component status: faithful_translation_with_unrolled_arithmetic
Statement: BlockDeg plus the base-monomial residues cancels the localizer degree and gives q_x(dP-deg b)_+<=G2d<=2a. Distinct previous-frame distances produce Delta_j<=3a/p^g with no factor r. WT2 — Signed conjugated-torus calculus for all needed first-order operators
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For a letter in a prefix, vector multiplication/derivative have minimum-order losses0/1 and maximum-order increases1/0; covectors have the reversed costs. Coordinate Euler has cost1 for either sign and either order. A letter outside the prefix has cost0. The proof is the exact chain rule for A(t)=g diag(t) g^(-1), whose entries use exponents0,1 and whose inverse uses0,-1.
Assumptions: ["Polynomial signed vector/covector substitution, with the generic matrix inverted in its coordinate ring."]
Depends on: ["WT1"]
Source relation: The source proves a more general divided-Taylor filtration theorem. The report gives a shorter complete chain-rule proof of exactly its first-order consequences needed here. Euler costs one because one signed factor costs zero.

WT3 — Exact residue/carry identities before and after the frame digit split
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: For q>=1, L_rho(partial H)=((rho+1)Id+q y partial_y)L_(rho+1)H for rho<q-1, and q partial_y L_0 H for rho=q-1. Also L_rho(XH)=L_(rho-1)H for rho>0 and y L_(q-1)H for rho=0. After block selection carry terms use input degree d+1 or d-1; multiplication into output degree0 vanishes. These identities apply both to levImg and to Fdig; an extra Fdig Euler term occurs only at a vector frame letter.

WT4 — Plane chain and link transport with one unit of cutoff loss
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The XXg plane conditions are preserved by derivative, multiplication and coordinate Euler when affected input cutoffs exceed the target by one. Derivative has nonzero cost only for vector letters, multiplication only for covectors; frame-to-carry derivatives are handled by the exact digit formula. Euler therefore still has cost1. Degree0 and unaffected-prefix cases are included.
Assumptions: ["The explicit homogeneous degrees and ThDrop inequalities at every chain and imposed link."]
Depends on: ["WT1", "WT2", "WT3"]
Source relation: This proves the sign-sensitive plDer/plMul arguments and the Euler conclusion; it does not simply invoke PlDer/PlMul as black-box assumptions.

WT5 — Normal joint-type band and coefficient recombination
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: For D a coordinate derivative, multiplication or Euler, e_(kappa-prime) D e_kappa can be nonzero only if kappa-prime_(j,u),1<=kappa_(j,u),1+1_(x0 in NSet(j,u)) at every cut. A finite joint decomposition and coefficientwise linear recombination then prove the exact NoOpStep. D is not assumed to commute with the projectors.
Assumptions: ["Finite-dimensional rational split GL representations in characteristic zero are completely reducible and obey highest-weight dominance.", "All polynomial/coefficient decompositions used at a time are finite; out-of-range natural prefix indices are extended by the output tuple."]
Depends on: ["WT1", "WT2"]
Source relation: Commutation of nested-prefix type projectors and the generic maximum/type identification are proved in the report from the stated field-level background. No integral-projector denominator, lattice decomposition, or new representation-theoretic assertion is retained.

WT6 — Adjacent-prefix threshold comparison and the actual OneOpStep
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The max defining thStar is 1-Lipschitz in the relevant adjacent normal first weights. Their transition indicators at u+1 and u-1 are bounded by the physical touch cost at u. Hence one physical derivative or multiplication adds cost1*delta(s), and X_(s,a)partial_(s,b) adds exactly2*delta(s) to the allowed loss. Universal degree-block quantifiers justify every intermediate degree update.

WT7 — Per-position word loss and exact numerical absorption for C>=16
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The actual list condition gives0<=wordLoss<=2*#letters(j)*c0<=2*N1*c0. FramesOK implies Bo>=a/p^G-prime because oldest is a selected position in the same window. WeightHyp gives flatDeg>=a. With Q=p^G-prime and cP=cStar+r*N*c0+2*r*n*cpp, Hyps gives C*k^3*r^2*N*Q^5*cP*Y<=a and N1^2<=r*N. For C>=16 these imply a>=16*N1*c0*Y*k^2*Q and sl>=16*N1*c0, including the exact floor. Thus wordLoss<=sl/8.
Assumptions: ["The actual FramesOK/Hyps/WeightHyp parameter inequalities, C>=16 and at mostc0 operators at EACH selected position.", "N=#TT, k=r+K, Q=p^G-prime; the physical frame window has cardinality<=N1 and span<G-prime."]
Depends on: ["WT1"]
Source relation: The report derives the needed slack inequality explicitly. It does not leave WordBoundStep or Bo_ge as a new input, does not misread c0 as a total word-length bound, and does not omit the floor.

PG3 — Weighted Fock lattices, algebraic orders and actual cutoff projectors
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The lattice b(F)>=0 is full, torus-graded and divided-power stable for arbitrary ramification, by the half-sum of two binomial valuations. Apply the companion IW4 to the S-letter weight interval [-D_S,D_S], using the difference of the same coordinate in two weights <=2D_S. The cutoff ord_S>=theta is the sum of isotypic components with last highest weight>=ceil(theta). Its Fock projector is selfadjoint; nested/disjoint cutoff projectors commute. Rescaling by p^ceil(-b(F)) gives weighted loss<=r^2(log_p(2T+r)+1). The V2 order calculus and binomial-operator degree costs are proved directly.
Assumptions: ["Universal isotypic-projector lattice bound IW4, with its exact coordinate-weight difference hypothesis.", "Standard characteristic-zero complete reducibility, highest-weight classification and rationality of the signed polynomial representation.", "The source DVR and degree hypotheses of PG1."]
Depends on: ["PG1"]
Source relation: This fragment proves the specialization and commutation/adjoint statements; IW4 supplies the universal denominator theorem in a companion proof. Weighted valuations need not be attained in the value group, so the rescaling loss1 is explicitly retained.

PG4 — A detected integral polynomial with the original link constraints
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Choose a coefficient attaining b(F)=0, project its monomial onto all original link cutoffs, approximate gamma^(-1) by a degree<=6h integral binomial polynomial and multiply by p^ceil(n0+Dl-v_p(alpha!)/2). This gives integral H with link loss6h and v(<F,Gamma H>)<=n0+Dl+1. The approximation error has strictly larger valuation and cannot cancel the detected coefficient.

PG5 — Marked path columns give the actual model lift
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Expand in the integral prefix-adapted signed path-column basis. Mark columns containing a base letter; only in those columns move frame indices m>0 to tangent variables. Tangent degree is bounded by the number of marked columns<=dLL. Unmarked columns have nonpositive colVal and no variables in the renamed link, so the original prefix order lower bounds survive. Injective renaming preserves each column Gauss valuation and its multiplicativity proves integrality of the full renamed product. Digit-split the remaining labels to obtain integral good Z with phi Z=H and no further link loss.
Assumptions: ["The exact integral signed path-column basis, prefix support adaptation, multilinearity and column-order clauses stated in report section6; these are shared with IP.", "The input H is integral, has the prescribed multidegrees and satisfies the link cutoffs."]
Depends on: ["PG3", "PG4"]
Source relation: The downstream lifting map and all its constraints are proved here. The proof status of the integral prefix-adapted basis remains the proof status of the companion IP theorem; it is not silently discharged by calling this map a lift.

PG6 — The joint chain projector has controlled coefficients and preserves every label/tangent block
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Form the product of the weakened chain cutoff projectors. Its sets are nested within segments, disjoint across segments, and contained in or disjoint from every relevant link set. It therefore preserves links. Euler commutation fixes every outside label/tangent exponent. On good x^zeta it has b>=v_p(zeta!)/2-Dm; within the resulting block factorial valuations differ by at most kp, so all coefficients are >=-Dm-kp/2. Hence p^ceil(Dm+kp/2) clears its coefficients on integral good inputs.
Assumptions: ["The cutoff projector construction and bounds in PG3.", "The good-exponent conditions and actual chain/link letter sets of PG1."]
Depends on: ["PG1", "PG3"]
Source relation: The factorial comparison uses full fixed individual model-letter degrees and fixed outside coordinate exponents; it is not an arbitrary projection on an ungraded lattice.

PG7 — Conjugated derivatives retain the weakened chains modulo p^h
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: For a tangent exponent M supported on frames with each frame degree<=dLL, every digit component of Gamma^(-1) partial^[M](Gamma F) is Q+E with weakened chain levels theta-s and coefficient valuation(E)>=h-n0. The two unit approximations cost12h total. The derivative cost at a chain is the sum over predecessor frames of |M_t|/P_t+h. The model slope hypothesis13 bounds that total by s.
Assumptions: ["The data gamma and gamma^(-1) approximations.", "The input F has b(F)>=0 and every digit component satisfies the original chains.", "The exact tangent degree caps and slope inequalities of PG1."]
Depends on: ["PG1", "PG2", "PG3"]
Source relation: The error invariant is preserved under each integral approximation and divided derivative, so the number of frame operations introduces no additional coefficient-valuation loss.

PG8 — Explicit factorial-unit conjugation and construction of Omega

Statement: On a good exponent zeta with collapsed exponent A and tangent M, A!M!=C_B gamma_dig(zeta) zeta!, with C_B=product(P_t!)^(carry degree_t), constant on a label/tangent block. Approximate gamma_*=gamma(A)gamma_dig and its inverse by integral diagonal g_plus,g_minus modulo p^h, each with order cost<=12h. Omega=diag(g_minus) Pi diag(g_plus) preserves goodness, has chain loss12h and additional link loss24h, and becomes coefficient-integral after p^ceil(Dm+kp/2).
Assumptions: ["The factorial-unit identity, unit property and integral Mahler/binomial approximations supplied by the companion DT proof.", "The original gamma input of SignedChainData.", "The chain projector PG6 and order calculus PG3."]
Depends on: ["PG1", "PG3", "PG6"]
Source relation: Uses the source degree6h bounds, even when the companion DT proof supplies stronger ones. The explicit C_B simplifies the more general source kapC after its actual constants are inserted.

PG9 — The block factorial cancellation proves near-invariance of the Gram value
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: The exact identity Lambda(x^zeta)=C_B gamma_*(zeta)(Gamma^(-1)partial^[M]Gamma F)_A zeta! converts Lambda into a blockwise Fock pairing with the conjugated derivative. Its chain-compatible part is fixed by Pi and cancels. Both v(C_B)+v_p(zeta!) and v(C_B)+v_p(zetaPrime!) are >=2n0-2kp; averaging combines this with the projector coefficient bound and error>=h-n0 to give v(Lambda(Omega Z)-Lambda(Z))>=h+n0-2kp-Dm for integral good Z.
Assumptions: ["All construction hypotheses of PG6-PG8.", "Fixed label/tangent blocks, so M and C_B are unchanged under the projector."]
Depends on: ["PG3", "PG6", "PG7", "PG8"]
Source relation: The source uses a two-case comparison of the two factorial valuations. The report replaces it by averaging the two exact lower bounds. This is an independent short simplification of the actual error proof, not a newly assumed estimate.

PG10 — ProjectionDerivativeEstimate is obtained with R equal to zero
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: Take the constructed Z and G=p^N2 Omega Z, R=0, N2=ceil(Dm+kp/2). The pairing error has strictly larger valuation than Lambda(Z), so detection survives. Since kp>=1, v(Lambda(G))<=n0+Dm+Dl+3kp; integrality gives b(phi G)>=n0-kp/2>=n0-kp. All monomials have the prescribed substituted multidegree. h<=2c gives exactly chain loss24c and link loss60c, with CH>=26 and CE=2.
Assumptions: ["The exact datum, order, depth and valuation assumptions in PG1.", "The companion representation and digit lemmas as recorded explicitly in PG11."]
Depends on: ["PG1", "PG4", "PG5", "PG6", "PG7", "PG8", "PG9", "PG11"]

Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For positive t_i and T=sum(t_i), the sum over 0<=u_1<...<u_m<b of product u_i^t_i is an integer-valued rational polynomial of degree at most T+m<=2T, hence has integral Newton coefficients.

Depends on: []

DT2 — Filtered finite-product approximation
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: If F(u)=1+sum a_t u^t with a_t in p^t Z_(p), the finite product over u<b has a binomial-polynomial approximation modulo p^c of degree at most 2(c-1). Total-grade truncation preserves this bound for products over arbitrarily many variables; inverse linear-unit products obey it too.
Assumptions: []
Depends on: ["DT1"]
Source relation: New finite-product argument, valid for every prime. Finite-precision expansions avoid an unstated infinite-product convergence claim.

DT3 — Exact factorial factorization into linear units
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For P=p^g and 0<=rho<P, gamma=(rho+Pb)!/(rho! b! (P!)^b) equals product_(i<=rho)(1+Pb/i) times product_(ell=1..g,u<b,1<=a<=p^ell,p nondividing a)(1+p^ell u/a). Each nonconstant linear coefficient belongs to p Z_(p), so gamma is a unit.
Assumptions: []
Depends on: []
Source relation: Exact factorization proved by stripping multiples of p from factorials; gamma is the literal source gamR.

CG1 — Actual paired-path basis, saturation, and reduction of XX′
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For any domain R, the source XX′ is the span of exactly the integral paired Psi basis indexed by segPairs. The normal-order projector keeps or kills each whole paired multidegree block. Therefore XX′ over O is saturated, its reduction is XX′ over the residue field, and total-letter-degree projection preserves it. This proves the first, third and sixth NestedTypeBound clauses used in the lift and RestLam.
Assumptions: ["The previously reconstructed universal integral signed-path basis and exact simultaneous prefix filtration adaptation, IP3–IP4.", "The source hypotheses valid frame, segN+r<=K and nonnegative integer margins are retained in application. The basis argument itself works without the latter two restrictions."]
Depends on: ["IP3", "IP4"]
Source relation: Direct proof of the needed three clauses from the common integral basis. The larger package fourth clause, a characteristic-zero joint-isotypic characterization, is neither assumed nor claimed here. Companion LA may use the actual saturation consequence.

CG2 — Literal coarse objects and Euclidean splitting of the coarse label
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The source coarse generator and segment modules are preserved exactly. Unique late representatives modulo the period give ell=ell0+p^dist e, with fine label ell0 and every local exponent e<P_j. This yields the exact product identity for monomials. It needs no injection on an entire overlapping segment.
Assumptions: ["Literal Dat.Hyp, defined in CG9 source references; all source natural-number subtractions and cutoffs are retained."]
Depends on: []
Source relation: The terminal-frame exponent restriction in Mj remains in the definition but is not used by the congruence proof. Variables outside TT remain in ell0; the required final zero degrees outside TT are supplied by the actual homogeneous-generator condition.

CG3 — Determinant degree loss and exact coarse power scale
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Every residue occurs at most twice in all segment letter sets, and each weighted determinant-row contribution is <=2a/(k²Y), giving E_t<=4Ns*a/(k²Y). The actual numerical hypotheses imply E_t<=a/40, E0<=a/32, a′>=0.9deg on TT and E<=d everywhere. With P_j=p^R_j, T_j>=4p(E0+mStar+1), P_j<=T_j<pP_j, P_j>mStar, and 8Yk²Ns*p^dist*P_j<=a.
Assumptions: ["Ck>=32 and the literal frame/size hypotheses, including P1 and P3."]
Depends on: ["CG2"]
Source relation: This is the same shared completed numerical result as RS2–RS3, whose elementary proof is recorded again for local readability; it is not an additional unproved interface. SD3 supplies nonvanishing separately and is not reproved.

CG4 — Internal coarse degrees and the oldest-letter dichotomy
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: A nonzero actual coarse generator has degree a′. An intermediate physical row occurs in only one segment, so a′=p^(dist+R)*b+label degree and the label bound yields b>a′/p^(dist+R)−k. The oldest of r vector predecessors of a late letter belongs either to the old frame or the intermediate set, exactly matching the two theta^c branches.
Assumptions: ["The coarse product u is nonzero; the u=0 case is handled separately in CG8.", "Each y_j has its declared whole-letter multidegree and satisfies the coarse allowed support."]
Depends on: ["CG2"]
Source relation: The degree equality uses fixed multihomogeneity, not an unjustified assertion that arbitrary product monomials cannot cancel. The integer-row and residue uniqueness distinction is preserved.

Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Both actual theta^c cases satisfy P_j(theta^c−kNs)>=theta. The proof uses c>=40kNs, q>=0.9c, b>q−k or floor(q)>q−1, retaining the old-frame offsets k+r+1 and m0=kNs+1. The oldest-letter gap gives P_j*o^c+kP_j<=o, with the exact source even/odd target constants10 and1.

CG6 — Canonical Frobenius product and all fine prefix and order bounds
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: For one allowed coarse paired path polynomial B=A0G0, reduction of D_j*expand_P(B)*X^e is A0^P*ellP*D_j times G0^P*ellN. Canonical coefficients lie in the prime field, so this identity is valid without inverse coefficient Frobenius. Signed label costs dS+dV<=kNsP and the individual determinant order s_x prove every fine gap, threshold and normal-order condition, with correct even/odd prefix indices and supports.
Assumptions: ["The residue field has characteristic p; canonical path polynomials have integral coefficients by their literal wedge/contraction construction.", "Local label e is late-supported and every exponent is <P_j."]
Depends on: ["CG1", "CG3", "CG4", "CG5", "IP3", "IP4"]
Source relation: The source four-premise wrapper is expanded into actual arithmetic and polynomial proofs. The general y expansion is coefficient-linear; no perfection of the residue field or false characteristic-zero Frobenius equivariance is used.

CG7 — Integral segment lift with the exact letter degree
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Expand the coarse y in the allowed integral path basis, lift each canonical product by CG6 and CG1, and preserve the original scalar coefficients. The exact z_j degree is P_j*b plus label degree plus determinant-row occurrence degree. Projecting the integral lift onto this whole-letter degree preserves XX′ and the residue congruence, proving SegmentReductionLiftsMultihomogeneous.
Assumptions: ["The segment y has its actual fixed whole-letter degree b."]
Depends on: ["CG1", "CG6"]
Source relation: The homogeneous-component argument is proved, not imported as an unexplained lifting theorem. A zero lift belongs to the prescribed homogeneous submodule and is allowed.

GP3 — Complete tail-sum recursion and persistence of a deficit
Historical/component status: complete_elementary_human_proof
Statement: Positive and reversed-negative suffix sums are bounded by suffix sums of the corresponding reverse-chronological preterminal degree lists. Active steps shift the deficit index by one; opposite-sign and terminal interlacing steps preserve it without loss.

GP9 — Antidiagonal specialization and integral independence
Historical/component status: complete_human_proof_using_IP_integral_path_basis
Statement: Killing off-antidiagonal terminal plane variables turns each actual plane path word into a unit times a frame monomial times its truncated-path word. Icut is standard and records every terminal column rise. The IP product basis gives specialized independence; taking the least auxiliary off-diagonal degree lifts it, and cancelling the nonzero common determinant-monomial gives RestInd.

JR3 — Separated edge blocks assemble without cancellation
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Primitive tests supported to p-adic accuracy on one incoming edge give primitive tests on the concatenation. If a divides p^D, then a+p^{D+1}z=a(1+pbz) also divides p^D, because 1+pbz is a unit. Applying JR2 yields LPprimeAt with n=sum_e n_e and matrix C=I.
Assumptions: ["p is nonzero and nonunit.", "All normalized edge pairings are integral.", "Every primitive combination on each edge has a dual test with value dividing p^D and p^{D+1} divisibility on other blocks.", "In the source w^2=p, cStar >= 2(D+1), BePerfect, and dominant weights imply the required off-block integrality."]
Depends on: ["JR1", "JR2", "JR12"]
Source relation: The per-edge tests are still inputs; this is the complete algebraic assembly of those tests.

JR4 — Matrix rank identity bounds bad Smith directions
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: If integral functionals and generators f_i of a sublattice of rank-d P satisfy C Phi u=qI_n, then some basis of P has at least n indices with q b_a in span(f_i). Split elementary divisors into a_i|q and a_i=q mu_i with mu_i in the maximal ideal; the latter yield qY, and rank(q(I-Y))=n forces at least n good terms. Under LPprime the bad count is <=kappa d.
Assumptions: ["P is a full finite free O-lattice.", "q is nonzero.", "All tested functionals are integral on P.", "For the source application the edge comparisons in JR12 and JR1 are in force."]
Depends on: ["JR1", "JR12"]
Source relation: The proof compresses the source jm_count argument by taking fraction-field ranks of the good-term matrix, instead of explicitly constructing an injective map.

JR5 — Neighbor evaluation isolates any good coordinate
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: For a free action on lattice tuples, delta sections are O-linear and equivariant. Applying y_v to the delta section at an incoming source yields the desired target term once, while all other terms lie in p^{D+1}M_B. Dividing the equivariant pointwise error by p^{D+1} yields an integral section. Tensoring with other integral factors gives p^D delta(tensor) in J_B+p^{D+1}M_B whenever one selected factor has a good index.
Assumptions: ["The acting groups have trivial stabilizers on valid lattice tuples.", "Coefficient lattice equivariance, finite neighbor sums, and the normalized integral neighbor-map inclusion hold.", "The off-target coefficient values lie in w^cStar times the appropriate target lattice, w^2=p, and cStar >= 4(D+1)."]
Depends on: ["JR1", "JR4", "JR12"]
Source relation: The evaluation/cancellation and pointwise-to-section divisibility are reconstructed; the underlying polynomial lattice covariance/integrality is retained separately as JR12.

JR6 — All-bad tensor labels have multiplicative cardinality
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: If factor v has d_v basis labels with <=kappa_v d_v bad labels, only tensors with every selected coordinate bad need remain exceptional. Their number is <=(product_{v in B}kappa_v)(product_v d_v); all other elementary tensors satisfy JR5. This is a tensor-coordinate argument, not a general bound for arbitrary intersections of bad subspaces.
Assumptions: ["Independent coefficient factors, realized by disjoint polynomial variable blocks.", "Integral generating lists of length d_v in each factor, with the selected good/bad properties.", "kappa_v is nonnegative for the global application."]
Depends on: ["JR4", "JR5"]

JR7 — Orbit globalization and Nakayama give the exact RestJ interface
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Delta-extend the all-bad tensors over finitely many orbits. Base tensor delta sections are independent by evaluation, so |Omega| product_v d_v <= dna. Their exceptional union has cardinal <=dna product kappa. The local decompositions give p^D M_B <=T+p^{D+1}M_B, with T=J_B+span(C_B); Nakayama gives p^D M_B<=T and hence the exported p^{D+1} inclusion. restJAll and theta_kernel_expansion assemble these proved inputs with the separate walk.
Assumptions: ["Finite orbit set; trivial stabilizers; coefficient lattices full and equivariant.", "M_B is a finite O-module and lies in Mna.", "p lies in the maximal ideal.", "All kappas are nonnegative."]
Depends on: ["JR5", "JR6", "JR12"]
Source relation: dna is the FULL function-module rank, not the retained ramified rank. The lattice walk and the elementary-divisor tail-to-index conversion are not rederived in this fragment.

Historical/component status: faithful_translation

Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Sort all marked complete-tile indices s_a and define B_j=n floor(j/J)+ell*s_(j mod J). The next positive cyclic marked-index distance is <=M+1. The wrap adds exactly n-floor(n/ell)*ell, proving ell<=B_(j+1)-B_j<(M+2)ell, periodicity and coverage: the full bf_Seq statement.
Assumptions: ["n=n'>0 is even; r>=2; the actual application has L1>=1.", "The explicitly expanded OrbitHyp, or the stated weaker OrbitRaw data, is supplied. No orbit-abundance premise is inferred from the construction."]

FG3 — Unique lifted cell tops, parity, isolation and periodicity
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Each marked tile has exactly 3r increasing even selected points a_(j,v) in [B_j+(2v+1)u,B_j+(2v+2)u). OR1 — A partial-prefix determinant twist is a rank-one update
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For r distinct selected vector rows and every prefix or arbitrary letter subset S′, the generic conjugate cocharacter changes the selected matrix by a rank-one update. Its determinant is affine in t with minimum exponent <=1. Hence val_S′(D_A^m H)<=val_S′(H)+m, including the zero case.
Assumptions: ["Any coefficient field, r>0, distinct chosen vector letters; no characteristic-zero or infinite-field assumption."]
Depends on: []
Source relation: This supplies a direct proof of the second clause of FieldMultidegreeDivisibility. That interface is a conclusion here, not a hypothesis.

OR2 — Generic singular specialization forces all determinant powers integrally
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For a letter-multihomogeneous polynomial, minimum prefix weight theta exceeding the degree B in other selected vector letters forces D_A^(theta−B) divisibility over every field. The proof uses the generic determinant prime and a kernel-adapted cocharacter; quotient degree and OR1 permit iteration. Unit-leading-coefficient division descends the quotient to every integral domain, preserving all prefix bounds.
Assumptions: ["Finite signed letter family over a field, or an integral domain after fraction-field extension.", "All chosen determinant rows are distinct vectors lying in the division subset; F is letter-multihomogeneous."]
Depends on: ["OR1"]
Source relation: Proves the previously abstract hE input itself. The generic determinant irreducibility proof is included and works in every characteristic; the integral descent does not require the base domain to be a UFD.

OR3 — Overlapping tasks and the literal segment divisor
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: A finite list of determinant tasks of total exponent T can be extracted if every initial task prefix has minimum at least its other-vector degree plus T. Each quotient has weakly smaller degrees and every prefix loses at most T. For actual segments the tasks are one recent-r-even determinant per late letter plus the preceding-frame determinant; their total cost is <=mStar, and their quotient satisfies exactly MGen0.
Assumptions: ["The exact Valid frame, even positive n′, r,K>0, and a late letter.", "The per-task strict-prefix valuation inequality; OR4–OR5 supply it in the actual application."]
Depends on: ["OR1", "OR2", "FG7"]
Source relation: The old-frame task uses a prefix containing only those r rows and hence has other-vector degree zero. All selected rows lie inside the segment; no default Arow branch is used. This proves dv_segment rather than merely invoking its hE premise.

OR4 — The actual one-sided other-vector degree is at most Bo/80
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Every even predecessor outside the r nearest ones is before the oldest of them and lies in the old frame or intermediate letter set. Its even distance is 2h for a distinct h>=1. The one-sided total-degree upper bound gives other degree <=2.02 Bo/(p^2−1)<=Bo/80 for p>=13, with no lower approximation assumption.
Assumptions: ["p>=13, even positive n′, r>=2, Valid frame; a<=deg_s<=2a on TT.", "Only d_y<=1.01 levDeg(y) on old-frame and intermediate letters is assumed."]
Depends on: ["FG7"]
Source relation: The finite sum is bounded by the full geometric series over distinct positive even distances. This proves the outgoing RestGeomU version, not just the absolute-error RestGeom statement.

OR5 — Explicit C>=100 extraction margin for the actual data
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: From the exact mStar definition, alphaMax<=1+rkQ, N1<=k and r,k>=2, one has mStar<=8rk²QcP. The actual size bound a>=Ck³r²NQ⁵cPY and oldest degree Bo>=a/Q imply mStar<=Bo/100 for C>=100. The exact floor slack is <=Bo/8, so Bo/2−sl>=Bo/80+mStar. Thus every actual MGen factors through Dv and MGen0.
Assumptions: ["r,k>=2, Y>=r, N>=1, Q>=1, cP>=1, N1<=k, alphaMax<=1+rkQ.", "Valid frame span z_j−f_(j−1,0)<=G′ and Q=p^G′.", "a>=Ck³r²NQ⁵cPY with C>=100 and a<=deg_s<=2a on TT."]
Depends on: ["OR3", "OR4", "FG7", "CP1"]
Source relation: This supplies the exact actual application with an explicit constant and weaker needed margin. It does not claim an optimized universal OneSidedLemma4 constant triple. No mStar<=sl premise or dropped floor is used.

OR6 — Whole-letter projection gives RestModel and integral quotient symbols
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Projecting the defining XX′ product span to fixed whole-letter degrees gives a finite integral sum of exact MGen products: generic substitution preserves each letter degree and its prefix bounds. The final order-support intersection is only forgotten for this inclusion. OR5 and completed IP6/IP11 then give xi=Dv xi′ with phi(xi′) in the actual symbol algebra.
Assumptions: ["The exact XX′ membership and whole-letter homogeneity of the outgoing xi family.", "The already reconstructed integral path-generator spanning and image statements IP6/IP11."]
Depends on: ["OR5", "IP3", "IP4", "IP6", "IP11"]
Source relation: No integral irreducible decomposition or termwise factorization of the final XX′ support intersection is asserted. The inclusion into MGen follows directly from homogeneous projection.

OR7 — The literal RestPh congruence and residual exponent arithmetic
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: Universal Frobenius determinant congruence modulo p and the binomial split give phi(Dseg_x)^m1 divisible modulo p^c by D_barx^(m1−c), and similarly the old-frame factor. Late intervals cover each TT residue once; cyclic frame reindexing and m1−c=(2Q+3)c+kQ, m2−c=c(alphaMax+1) yield product phi(Dv)=fixedSymbolFactor(c) DkQ H+p^cY with H integral tangential and Y integral.
Assumptions: ["The exact Ctx frame/chart/coefficients, any nonnegative c, and m1/m2 as defined.", "Frobenius is used as a ring endomorphism modulo p; no arbitrary coefficient is asserted fixed under it."]
Depends on: ["FG7"]
Source relation: This proves the actual outgoing multiplier identity. It keeps the p^c error and nonnegative residual powers c(alphaMax−alpha_j); it is not replaced by the ordinary SPtrue multiplier assertion.

GG1 — Literal signed coefficient, highest-vector and graded initial lattices
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The actual grLat is the image in_e(F_e M_w), not its saturation. The form is Fock/prod_i(d_i!), so every monomial diagonal is a reciprocal product of integer multinomials.
Assumptions: ["p is prime, coefficients are Q_p with coefficient lattice Z_p, and v_p(p)=1.", "The signed word has K+1 letters, r>=2 coordinates, rho=r-1, and its final letter is a vector.", "Each letter has a fixed nonnegative integral degree; there are finitely many prefix constraints with thresholds in Z union {infinity}.", "Standard characteristic-zero split-GL highest-weight theory and elementary DVR/Smith theory are declared background. Integral denominator statements use the already proved IW1-IW4."]
Depends on: []
Source relation: The coefficient image retains the factor z^e. Saturation is not inserted into its definition.

GG2 — Exact integral prefix projectors, highest projection and multiplicity-safe Weyl generation
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: The signed prefix coordinate width is at most D, yielding HypP, HypE and HypW with e1=binom(r,2)Nat.log_p(D+r-1). HypE is the matching smaller-group type projector on a fixed full weight. Highest-vector generation works on an entire isotypic module with multiplicities and requires no integral irreducible splitting.
Assumptions: ["p is prime, coefficients are Q_p with coefficient lattice Z_p, and v_p(p)=1.", "The signed word has K+1 letters, r>=2 coordinates, rho=r-1, and its final letter is a vector.", "Each letter has a fixed nonnegative integral degree; there are finitely many prefix constraints with thresholds in Z union {infinity}.", "Standard characteristic-zero split-GL highest-weight theory and elementary DVR/Smith theory are declared background. Integral denominator statements use the already proved IW1-IW4."]
Depends on: ["GG1", "IW1", "IW2", "IW3", "IW4"]
Source relation: The multiplicity-space extension of IW3 is proved explicitly. The Hom height is the difference of two weights at one coordinate, not a difference of coordinates within one weight.

GG3 — Explicit auxiliary GL action, integral divided powers and finite weight width
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: The literal XSp direct sum is stable under EX. A direct first-weight argument bypasses rational-surjectivity/Omega injectivity. Generic W-coordinate evaluation gives o<=c+D_early, and all auxiliary weight coordinates lie in [-D_early,c+2D_early], so the width is <=4D. The formal U-flow proves root divided-power integrality for every integer c.
Assumptions: ["p is prime, coefficients are Q_p with coefficient lattice Z_p, and v_p(p)=1.", "The signed word has K+1 letters, r>=2 coordinates, rho=r-1, and its final letter is a vector.", "Each letter has a fixed nonnegative integral degree; there are finitely many prefix constraints with thresholds in Z union {infinity}.", "Standard characteristic-zero split-GL highest-weight theory and elementary DVR/Smith theory are declared background. Integral denominator statements use the already proved IW1-IW4."]
Depends on: ["GG1", "GG2"]
Source relation: The complete proof checks the actual XSp cutoffs directly. Neither x_lift nor Omega injectivity is a remaining input. The formal exponential is a new compact proof of the exact source divided-power assertion; it is not claimed formalized.

GG4 — The actual restriction-image lattice lifts after precisely two IW losses
Historical/component status: faithful_translation
Statement: For every integral x in the literal XSp at the original last degree, an integral h in the literal Y has h|_(z=0)=p^(2D4)x. M2 is divided-power stable and contains all integral auxiliary highest vectors, which have last degree zero. Type isolation and highest generation each cost D4, and extracting the original degree yields the actual lift.
Assumptions: ["p is prime, coefficients are Q_p with coefficient lattice Z_p, and v_p(p)=1.", "The signed word has K+1 letters, r>=2 coordinates, rho=r-1, and its final letter is a vector.", "Each letter has a fixed nonnegative integral degree; there are finitely many prefix constraints with thresholds in Z union {infinity}.", "Standard characteristic-zero split-GL highest-weight theory and elementary DVR/Smith theory are declared background. Integral denominator statements use the already proved IW1-IW4."]
Depends on: ["GG1", "GG2", "GG3"]
Source relation: The source's c0=2D4 is retained exactly. This proves controlled lifting, not exact integral surjectivity or saturation of M2. No separate rational-surjectivity input is used.

GG5 — Exact order stripping and saturation control for the actual graded image
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: Multiplication by z^e shifts only the final degree, rho weight, and full-prefix thresholds. The rational graded span is z^e XH for the reduced data. Projecting the actual integral lift to full weight and smaller-group highest vectors proves p^(e1+2D4)(V_e intersect Z_p[X]) subset grLat.
Assumptions: ["p is prime, coefficients are Q_p with coefficient lattice Z_p, and v_p(p)=1.", "The signed word has K+1 letters, r>=2 coordinates, rho=r-1, and its final letter is a vector.", "Each letter has a fixed nonnegative integral degree; there are finitely many prefix constraints with thresholds in Z union {infinity}.", "Standard characteristic-zero split-GL highest-weight theory and elementary DVR/Smith theory are declared background. Integral denominator statements use the already proved IW1-IW4."]
Depends on: ["GG1", "GG2", "GG4"]
Source relation: Generic first-weight Laurent-degree additivity proves both directions of the cutoff shift. Initial coefficients retain z^e; actual saturation cost b=e1+2D4 is proved, not assumed.

GG6 — Orthogonal graded projection with cost (K+1)e1 and exact zero-prefix handling
Historical/component status: derived_simplification
Statement: For K>=1 there is a rational Fock-orthogonal projection onto V_e, integral after p^((K+1)e1). The K+2 type projections commute; prefix0 and prefix1 are identity or zero, leaving K paid projections and one highest projection. For K=0 the actual nonzero graded lattice is a monomial line with Gram entry 1/binom(d,e).
Assumptions: ["p is prime, coefficients are Q_p with coefficient lattice Z_p, and v_p(p)=1.", "The signed word has K+1 letters, r>=2 coordinates, rho=r-1, and its final letter is a vector.", "Each letter has a fixed nonnegative integral degree; there are finitely many prefix constraints with thresholds in Z union {infinity}.", "Standard characteristic-zero split-GL highest-weight theory and elementary DVR/Smith theory are declared background. Integral denominator statements use the already proved IW1-IW4."]
Depends on: ["GG1", "GG2", "GG5"]
Source relation: The positive-K cost is exactly the source's improved exponent. The direct K=0 monomial calculation is stronger than the generic source estimate and is not used to alter downstream constants.
